# elenchus-mcp 0.13.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/elenchus-mcp/0.13.0

# elenchus-mcp

⚠️

Experimental.elenchus is mostly an AI-built experiment — written with the help of a small local model (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf) and various Claude models, in roughly equal measure. Expect non-professional design choices, rough edges, broken behavior, or mistakes. Use it at your own risk.

Part of [elenchus](https://github.com/m62624/elenchus): a
[Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that exposes its
consistency checker to AI agents.

Transport: **stdio, newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0** (one message per line).
Hand-rolled with `serde_json` — no MCP SDK dependency.

## CLI or MCP — which one?

Both let an LLM run elenchus; the output is the same either way. The difference is setup cost:

- **CLI (**—- `elenchus-cli`)- `elenchus-cli <file>`or- `elenchus-cli --text "…"`from the shell. Works in every harness that can run shell commands (Claude Code, any CI pipeline, terminal).- **Recommended: it needs no extra configuration, so if your harness can run shell commands, use the CLI.**
- **MCP server (**— speaks stdio JSON-RPC. Worth the extra setup only when your harness natively supports MCP and you'd rather not (or can't) run a shell. Same output, more to configure.- `elenchus-mcp`)

The **skill** ([ skill/SKILL.md](https://github.com/m62624/elenchus/blob/main/skill/SKILL.md)) is adapted for both — it
works identically whether the agent calls

`elenchus-cli` via the CLI or via the MCP tool.## Tool

`elenchus_check` — check a `.vrf` program for logical consistency.

Entry is **either** an inline `program` **or** a filesystem `path` (exactly one).

| Argument | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `program` | string | an inline `.vrf`program (opens with`DOMAIN`;`FACT`/`NOT`/`ASSUME`,`PREMISE`/`RULE`,`CHECK`, …) |
| `path` | string | a filesystem path the server reads instead (local server; resolves `IMPORT`s from disk) |
| `files` | object | in-memory `{ "path": "<.vrf text>" }`map that`program`'s`IMPORT`s resolve against |
| `values` | object | `{ "port": true|false }`bindings for`VAR`ports |
| `data` | object | `{ "name": "<PROVIDE text>" }`bindings for data-driven ports |
| `format` | `"human"`|`"json"` | output format, default `"json"` |
| `max_classes` | integer | on a syntax error, show at most this many error classes — one per keyword ( `0`or omitted = all) |
| `max_per_class` | integer | on a syntax error, show at most this many places within each class ( `0`or omitted = all) |
| `max_conflicts` | integer | safety valve — only set if a check hangs. Aborts with an error (no verdict) if the solver needs more SAT conflicts than this ( `0`or omitted = unlimited). Recommended:100000. |

The result is one of **CONSISTENT / WARNING / UNDERDETERMINED / CONFLICT**.
Treat anything other than CONSISTENT as *not done*: add the missing facts or
rethink the premises, then call again — iterate until CONSISTENT.

A **syntax error** comes back as a tool error (`isError: true`): the `text`
field carries the full diagnostic, **grouped by class** (one per keyword) — the
correct syntax and an example shown once per class, with every offending place
listed beneath. Every error is reported in one pass. By default you get all of
them; `max_classes` and `max_per_class` independently cap the two dimensions
(both default to all). The whole multi-line block is a single JSON string, so the
wire stays valid JSON.

If `max_conflicts` is exceeded, the tool returns `isError: true` with a one-line message — the check did not finish, no verdict.

## Run

```
$ elenchus-mcp        # speaks JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout
```
Example session (each line is one JSON-RPC message):

```
→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}
← {"id":1,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"capabilities":{"tools":{}},"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","serverInfo":{"name":"elenchus","version":"x.y.z"}}}
→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"elenchus_check","arguments":{"program":"DOMAIN d\nFACT x a\nNOT x a\nCHECK x\n"}}}
← {"id":2,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"status\":\"CONFLICT\", …}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}
```
(`serverInfo.version` is the **engine** version, not the npm/crate line.)

MIT — see [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE).

# elenchus-cli 0.13.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/elenchus-cli/0.13.0

# elenchus-cli

⚠️

Experimental.elenchus is mostly an AI-built experiment — written with the help of a small local model (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf) and various Claude models, in roughly equal measure. Expect non-professional design choices, rough edges, broken behavior, or mistakes. Use it at your own risk.

The command-line interface of [elenchus](https://github.com/m62624/elenchus), part of
that project. It reads a `.vrf` program (a file, inline text, or stdin), runs the
consistency check, and prints the verdict. A thin `std` wrapper over the engine crates
(`elenchus-parser` → `elenchus-compiler` → `elenchus-solver`).

The companion **skill** ([ skill/SKILL.md](https://github.com/m62624/elenchus/blob/main/skill/SKILL.md)) teaches an LLM agent
how to drive it end to end — the DSL, worked examples, and the iterate-to-CONSISTENT
loop. It works in any harness that can run shell tools.

## Usage

One input, three ways — a positional file, inline `--text`, or stdin `-`:

```
$ elenchus-cli path/to/program.vrf              # a file (IMPORTs resolve relative to it)
$ elenchus-cli --text "DOMAIN d
FACT x a
CHECK x"                                          # inline, multi-line
$ printf 'DOMAIN d\nFACT x a\nNOT x a\nCHECK x\n' | elenchus-cli -   # stdin, one line
$ elenchus-cli program.vrf --format json          # machine-readable, one line out
$ elenchus-cli broken.vrf --max-per-class 3       # cap places shown per error class
$ elenchus-cli slow.vrf --max-conflicts 100000    # safety valve (exit 3 if exceeded)
```
`--text` and a file are mutually exclusive; with no input at all the CLI prints help
instead of blocking on stdin. ** IMPORT resolves only for the file form** —

`--text`
and stdin are treated as a single source.Exit code doubles as a CI gate:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | CONSISTENT |
| 1 | UNDERDETERMINED or WARNING |
| 2 | CONFLICT, or a parse/compile error |
| 3 | `--max-conflicts`budget exceeded — the check didnotfinish, no verdict |

** --max-conflicts** — safety valve, only set if a check hangs. Aborts (exit 3, no verdict) if the solver needs more SAT conflicts than this (

`0` or omitted = unlimited). Recommended: **100000**.

## Output

**Human (default).** Here a gate whose consequent has not been established yet — the
premise cannot be checked, so the verdict is `WARNING` and the report says exactly
which atom is missing and how to supply it:

```
$ elenchus-cli ready.vrf
RESULT: WARNING
  WARNING   ready (PREMISE)  [ready.vrf:3]
      blocked by: web.svc tested
      fix: nothing determines `web.svc tested` — add `FACT web.svc tested` (or `NOT …`), or if a PREMISE's THEN is meant to establish it, make that PREMISE a RULE so it derives the value
SUMMARY: 0 conflicts, 0 underdetermined, 1 warnings, 0 derived
EXIT_CODE: 1
```
**JSON ( --format json)** — a single line, for tooling and agents. Here a CONSISTENT
run that forward-chained one derived fact:

```
```
### Syntax errors

A malformed program exits `2` and prints every error found in one pass, **grouped by
class** (one class per keyword): the correct syntax and a real example are shown *once
per class*, with each offending place listed beneath — line, caret, and the specific
problem.

```
$ elenchus-cli broken.vrf
RESULT: 1 syntax error in broken.vrf
THEN  (1 problem)
  syntax  : THEN <literal>
  example : THEN motor uses fast_path
    line 4, col 9 - THEN expects a literal: [NOT] <Subject> <predicate> [<object>]
      |     THEN
      |         ^
```
Two independent caps control the volume (both default to "all"):

| Flag | Caps | Footer when it hides something |
|---|---|---|
| `--max-classes N` | number of classes shown | `… and N more classes` |
| `--max-per-class N` | places shown within each class | `… and N more <keyword> problems` |

Set just one to cap that dimension and leave the other full; set both for full control.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE).

# elenchus_solver - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/elenchus-solver/0.13.0/elenchus_solver/

## Expand description

elenchus-solver — the inference interpreter (forward pass).

Consumes the [ Compiled](https://docs.rs/elenchus-compiler/0.13.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/elenchus_compiler/ir/struct.Compiled.html) IR from

`elenchus-compiler` and evaluates it under
three-valued Kleene logic (TRUE / FALSE / UNKNOWN, where UNKNOWN ≠ FALSE):- seed a model from confident `FACT`/`NOT`facts (and report`FACT X`+`NOT X`);
- forward-chain `RULE`s to a fixpoint, deriving facts (a derived value that contradicts an existing one is a CONFLICT);
- evaluate every `Impossible`clause (the desugared`PREMISE`s):- all literals forced TRUE → **CONFLICT**(the constraint is violated);
- some literal FALSE → satisfied → CONSISTENT;
- otherwise (no FALSE, an UNKNOWN remains): for implication premises this is a
**WARNING**(blocked by missing data), for list premises (EXCLUSIVE/FORBIDS/ ONEOF/ATLEAST) it is CONSISTENT (UNKNOWN means “no conflict yet”).

- all literals forced TRUE →

On `CHECK ... BIDIRECTIONAL` a **backward pass** also runs: the premises, rules
and confident facts are encoded as CNF and handed to a small in-crate CDCL SAT
core ([ sat](https://docs.rs/sat/index.html), replicating varisat’s algorithm) to count models — 0 means the
system is jointly unsatisfiable (a CONFLICT the forward pass may miss), ≥2
means an alternative model exists (

`UNDERDETERMINED`).[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use elenchus_solver::{Status, verify_source};
// `A has flying` fires the premise, but `A has wing` was never stated — so
// the engine cannot confirm the rule and reports WARNING (not CONFLICT).
let report = verify_source(
    "demo.vrf",
    "DOMAIN d\nFACT A has flying\nPREMISE w:\n    WHEN A has flying\n    THEN A has wing\n",
)
.unwrap();
assert_eq!(report.status, Status::Warning); // `A has wing` is UNKNOWN
println!("{report}"); // the full human report, ready to show a model
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [sat](https://docs.rs/sat/index.html)
- A compact, single-threaded CDCL SAT solver in `no_std`, replicating the core algorithm of varisat (jix/varisat) in a readable, lazy style.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Conflict](https://docs.rs/struct.Conflict.html)
- A violated constraint (or a fact-level contradiction).
- [Core](https://docs.rs/struct.CoreItem.html)- Item
- One construct named in an `Report::unsat_core``Report::retract`
- [Derived](https://docs.rs/struct.Derived.html)
- A fact produced by a `RULE`during forward chaining.
- [Diagnostics](https://docs.rs/struct.Diagnostics.html)
- Re-exported so library users handling a `CompileError::Parse``--max-errors`). Every syntax error from one parse, plus the source label for the header.
- [False](https://docs.rs/struct.FalseBelief.html)- Belief
- One `BELIEVES <agent> <literal>`whose claim the settled world model establishes FALSE — a false belief (the epistemic L6 layer). Because belief is non-factive (unlike`KNOWS`, where knowing a falsehood is a CONFLICT), this is not a contradiction in the world; it is surfaced as a visible but**informational**note (exit 0, like DEFEATED) naming who believes what against the facts. It never raises the verdict — neither to WARNING nor to CONFLICT.
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileResolver.html)- Resolver
- The filesystem-backed resolver (reads `IMPORT`s from disk). Only with`std`. A filesystem-backed resolver. Mirrors vsm-grammar’s`FileResolver`: relative imports resolve against the importing file’s directory, with manual`..`normalization (no canonicalization, to keep a virtual layout).
- [Fix](https://docs.rs/struct.Fix.html)
- One concrete, engine-checked repair the reader can apply, then re-run — the
engine’s answer to “CONFLICT, but *what do I change?*”. Purely advisory: applying it is the caller’s choice, and its presence never affects`Report::status``Report::exit_code`
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryResolver.html)- Resolver
- An in-memory resolver: serves sources from a name → content map. Pure
`no_std`. Mirrors vsm-grammar’s`MemoryResolver`.
- [Orphan](https://docs.rs/struct.OrphanFact.html)- Fact
- An advisory lint: a `FACT`/`NOT`/`ASSUME`whose atom appears in**no**`PREMISE`or`RULE`. Such an assertion is logically inert — nothing checks it and nothing is derived from it, so it can never produce a CONFLICT, WARNING or DERIVED. It is almost always a typo’d atom name or a leftover line.**Purely informational**— it never changes the verdict, the warning pool, or the exit code (a program full of orphans is still perfectly CONSISTENT).
- [Placeholder](https://docs.rs/struct.PlaceholderInfo.html)- Info
- A reporting record for one declared `VAR`port: its key, how it resolved, the value it took (if any), and where that value came from.
- [Port](https://docs.rs/struct.PortBinding.html)- Binding
- One external value bound to a port `key`, supplied from outside the program (CLI / API / a data file). The`origin`is a short human tag used both in the placeholders report and in a [`CompileError::PortConflict`] message.
- [Report](https://docs.rs/struct.Report.html)
- The result of solving, self-contained (atom ids already resolved to labels).
- [Similar](https://docs.rs/struct.SimilarAtoms.html)- Atoms
- An advisory hint that two atom names look like the same atom typed two
different ways (e.g. `is_rolled_back`vs`is rolled_back`).**Purely a suggestion**— it never changes the verdict, the warning pool, or the exit code. It exists to catch the silent-typo trap where a misspelling creates a new UNKNOWN atom that quietly never links to the rest of the program.
- [Solve](https://docs.rs/struct.SolveOptions.html)- Options
- Solve-time options for the `_opts`entry points.`Default`disables everything, making them behave exactly like their plain counterparts.
- [Trace](https://docs.rs/struct.TraceStep.html)- Step
- One link in a `Conflict`
- [Tried](https://docs.rs/struct.Tried.html)
- One `TRY <literal>`hypothesis and the engine’s checked verdict on it. Purely advisory: the candidate is never committed, so it never changes the verdict or exit code — it only reports what asserting it*would*do.
- [Unused](https://docs.rs/struct.UnusedImport.html)- Import
- An advisory record: a file `IMPORT`s a domain it never references. Such an import is inert — no`domain.atom`in that file mentions it, so removing it would not change the result. It is almost always a leftover or a forgotten`domain.`prefix.**Purely informational**— it never changes the verdict.
- [Warning](https://docs.rs/struct.Warning.html)
- A constraint that could not be checked because a needed atom is UNKNOWN.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- The engine’s verdict on one `TRY <literal>`hypothesis — whether asserting the supplied candidate would resolve the program’s open gap. Each is decided by a single side-solve (the program*plus*the candidate literal); the hypothesis is never committed to the model.
- [V3](https://docs.rs/enum.V3.html)
- Three-valued truth (Kleene). UNKNOWN is a first-class value, not hidden FALSE.
- [Verify](https://docs.rs/enum.VerifyError.html)- Error

# elenchus_compiler - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/elenchus-compiler/0.13.0/elenchus_compiler/

## Expand description

elenchus-compiler — compiles parsed elenchus DSL into a canonical clause IR.

This crate is **preparation, not solving**. It takes the AST (from
`elenchus-parser`) and produces a deterministic, solver-ready intermediate
representation:

- **atom interner**:- `(subject, predicate, object?)`→ dense- `u32`id, canonically sorted so ids (and any later enumeration) are deterministic;
- **desugaring**: surface CAPS sugar →- `Impossible`clauses (- `EXCLUSIVE`pairwise,- `WHEN…THEN`→- `Impossible([A, …, NOT C])`, etc.);
- **content-addressing**(sha256, mirroring vsm-guard’s CAS): identical clauses are deduped (idempotent —- `P ∧ P ≡ P`), and a named construct redefined with a different body is a- `PremiseRedefinition`error.

The actual reasoning (3-valued forward chaining, SAT, all-SAT, the WARNING
pool, the four results) lives in `elenchus-solver`. `IMPORT` resolution is a
source-agnostic [ Resolver](https://docs.rs/trait.Resolver.html) that flat-merges another source into the shared
atom universe (

[resolves imports;](https://docs.rs/fn.compile.html)

`compile`[leaves them pending).](https://docs.rs/fn.compile_source.html)

`compile_source`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use elenchus_compiler::compile_source;
// `ASSUME` lowers to a *soft* fact: the same atom universe as a `FACT`, but
// one the solver may retract. Here `x a` is asserted both ways (hard + soft).
let ir = compile_source("demo.vrf", "DOMAIN d\nFACT x a\nASSUME NOT x a\nCHECK x\n").unwrap();
assert_eq!(ir.facts.len(), 2);
assert!(ir.facts.iter().any(|f| f.soft)); // the ASSUME is the soft one
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [kw](https://docs.rs/kw/index.html)
- Re-exported so downstream crates name one source of truth: `Diagnostics``CompileError::Parse``kw``Origin::kind``kind`against`kw::PREMISE`, not a re-typed`"PREMISE"`). The CAPS spelling of every keyword — the one place each literal appears.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [AtomKey](https://docs.rs/struct.AtomKey.html)
- The identity of an atom: the `domain`plus the triple`(subject, predicate, object?)`, owned so it survives across merged sources. The domain is the leading sort key, so atoms group by domain; ordering is otherwise lexicographic → canonical. Two atoms with the same triple in*different*domains are distinct (no cross-domain unification).
- [Attribution](https://docs.rs/struct.Attribution.html)
- One `KNOWS`/`BELIEVES <agent> <literal>`attribution: the agent (a report-side label, not an atom), the claimed literal, whether it is factive (`KNOWS`), and the provenance. The solver checks the literal’s model value per agent — factive: FALSE → CONFLICT (you cannot know a falsehood), UNKNOWN → WARNING; non-factive: FALSE → an informational note (exit 0, a false belief), else silent — plus a per-agent coherence check (knowing φ and ¬φ → CONFLICT). It is**evaluative, not a constraint**: no clause, no fact, the agent never enters the SAT core.
- [Check](https://docs.rs/struct.Check.html)
- A `CHECK`query.
- [Clause](https://docs.rs/struct.Clause.html)
- An `Impossible`clause: the listed literals cannot all hold simultaneously.
- [Compiled](https://docs.rs/struct.Compiled.html)
- The compiled IR: the solver’s input.
- [Compiler](https://docs.rs/struct.Compiler.html)
- Accumulates statements from one or more sources, then interns + emits the IR.
- [Diagnostics](https://docs.rs/struct.Diagnostics.html)
- Re-exported so downstream crates name one source of truth: `Diagnostics``CompileError::Parse``kw``Origin::kind``kind`against`kw::PREMISE`, not a re-typed`"PREMISE"`). Every syntax error from one parse, plus the source label for the header.
- [Fact](https://docs.rs/struct.Fact.html)
- A confident fact (from `FACT`/`NOT`). Conflicting facts on the same atom are preserved (both kept) — the solver reports that as a CONFLICT.
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileResolver.html)- Resolver
- A filesystem-backed resolver. Mirrors vsm-grammar’s `FileResolver`: relative imports resolve against the importing file’s directory, with manual`..`normalization (no canonicalization, to keep a virtual layout).
- [Hypothesis](https://docs.rs/struct.Hypothesis.html)
- One `TRY <literal>`hypothesis: the candidate atom (with its polarity) and the provenance of the`TRY`. The solver adds this single literal to the program and re-solves, judging the outcome — it is**evaluative, not a constraint**: it emits no clause and no fact, so it never enters the model or affects the verdict.
- [Justification](https://docs.rs/struct.Justification.html)
- One `FACT … BECAUSE <ground>`justification: the belief atom, the ground it is claimed to rest on, and the provenance of the`BECAUSE`. The solver checks the ground’s model value (FALSE → CONFLICT, UNKNOWN → WARNING, TRUE → silent). It is**evaluative, not a constraint**— it emits no clause, so an UNKNOWN ground is reported rather than silently forced true.
- [Lit](https://docs.rs/struct.Lit.html)
- A literal as it appears *inside*an`Impossible`clause: an atom, optionally negated.`negated = true`means the literal is`NOT atom`.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryResolver.html)- Resolver
- An in-memory resolver: serves sources from a name → content map. Pure
`no_std`. Mirrors vsm-grammar’s`MemoryResolver`.
- [Origin](https://docs.rs/struct.Origin.html)
- Where a piece of IR came from — for readable conflict/warning pools.
- [Placeholder](https://docs.rs/struct.PlaceholderInfo.html)- Info
- A reporting record for one declared `VAR`port: its key, how it resolved, the value it took (if any), and where that value came from.
- [Port](https://docs.rs/struct.PortBinding.html)- Binding
- One external value bound to a port `key`, supplied from outside the program (CLI / API / a data file). The`origin`is a short human tag used both in the placeholders report and in a [`CompileError::PortConflict`] message.
- [Rule](https://docs.rs/struct.Rule.html)
- A forward-chaining rule (from `RULE`): if all antecedent literals hold, derive the consequent literals —*unless*an exception defeats it.
- [Unknown](https://docs.rs/struct.UnknownValue.html)- Value
- Details of a closed-world violation (see `CompileError::UnknownValue`
- [Unused](https://docs.rs/struct.UnusedImport.html)- Import
- An advisory record: a file `IMPORT`s a domain it never references. Such an import is inert — no`domain.atom`in that file mentions it, so removing it would not change the result. It is almost always a leftover or a forgotten`domain.`prefix.**Purely informational**— it never changes the verdict.
- [Unwitnessed](https://docs.rs/struct.UnwitnessedExists.html)- Exists
- An advisory record: an `EXISTS`premise that named no candidate — neither a`SET`(`IN`) nor a`WITNESS`. It cannot be checked (there is nothing to point at), so it grounds to no clause and is reported as a WARNING.**Advisory to the SAT core, but it does raise the verdict to WARNING**(a premise that could not be checked), matching an implication blocked by an UNKNOWN atom.

# elenchus_parser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/elenchus-parser/0.13.0/elenchus_parser/

## Expand description

elenchus-parser — parses the English-like elenchus DSL into an AST.

Style mirrors `vsm-parser`: zero-copy over `&str`, `nom` + `nom_locate`
for line/column tracking, and human-friendly syntax diagnostics. Syntax is
line/keyword-oriented (not S-expressions) so small models cannot trip on
parentheses or indentation.

Grammar (see docs/SPEC.md, “Grammar (EBNF)”):

- statements are newline-terminated; indentation is cosmetic, not significant;
- keywords are ALWAYS CAPS (ASCII); identifiers are content (case-sensitive,
verbatim, any-script letters — e.g. `условие`,`名前`);
- block boundaries (PREMISE/RULE bodies) are found by keywords, never by indent.

On error, [ parse](https://docs.rs/fn.parse.html) returns

[:](https://docs.rs/diag/struct.Diagnostics.html)

`Diagnostics`*every*syntax error from one pass, each rendered as a caret block with the keyword’s correct syntax (see

[and [](https://docs.rs/diag/index.html)

`diag``syntax`]).The crate is split into focused modules — [ ast](https://docs.rs/ast/index.html) (the tree),

[(the single keyword table: spellings, roles, syntax cards),](https://docs.rs/keywords/index.html)

`keywords`[(error rendering), and](https://docs.rs/diag/index.html)

`diag``grammar` (the nom parser + recovering driver) — re-exported
here as a flat public surface.[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use elenchus_parser::{Statement, parse};
// One statement per line; the result is a flat list of `Statement`s.
let program = parse("FACT socrates is human\nCHECK socrates\n").unwrap();
assert_eq!(program.statements.len(), 2);
assert!(matches!(program.statements[0], Statement::Fact { .. }));
```

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [ast](https://docs.rs/ast/index.html)

# RustDiff

Semantic JSON, XML & SQL diff tool with a native GTK4 + Libadwaita desktop UI.

Language: **English** | [Espanol](https://docs.rs/README.es.md)

## Features

- Semantic JSON, XML & SQL diff (objects, arrays, XML nodes, attributes, text, and SQL statements)
- Welcome screen with guided comparison flow (single editor initially)
- Side-by-side editors with syntax highlighting
- **Busqueda en editores**(- `Ctrl+F`) con navegacion siguiente/anterior y wrap-around
- Auto compare while typing (debounced) + manual compare
- Difference table with filters and click-to-jump navigation
- Export to `.txt`and styled`.html`
- Session history stored in SQLite (paginated, searchable)

# turnkey_proofs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/turnkey_proofs/0.9.0/turnkey_proofs/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#turnkey_proofs)`turnkey_proofs`

This crate contains utilities to parse and verify Turnkey secure enclave proofs. To learn more about Turnkey verification, check out our [Turnkey Verified docs](https://docs.turnkey.com/security/turnkey-verified). As outlined in that doc, there are two types of proofs:

- App proofs, signing structured data with enclave ephemeral keys.
- Boot proofs, which are proofs that a given enclave was provisioned correctly. Boot proofs reference via their `public_key`field the enclave ephemeral key. This links App and Boot proofs together.

[§](https://docs.rs#boot-proofs)Boot proofs

Boot Proof: a proof that a particular AWS Nitro Enclave booted with a particular approved manifest envelope and configuration.

A boot proof contains

- AWS attestation document, which contains PCR measurements, a certification chain that proves the document was signed by AWS’s root cert, a public key which is the ephemeral key unique to this particular enclave, and `user_data`containing the approved QOS manifest hash.
- A QOS manifest and manifest envelope. The envelope is the authoritative source for the schema-aware manifest hash and approval set; the standalone manifest is checked for consistency with that envelope.

Resources on AWS Nitro Enclaves, attestations, and verifying attestations can be found at the following:

- [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/nitro-enclave.html](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/nitro-enclave.html)
- [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/set-up-attestation.html](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/set-up-attestation.html)
- [https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/validating-attestation-documents-produced-by-aws-nitro-enclaves/](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/validating-attestation-documents-produced-by-aws-nitro-enclaves/)
- [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/verify-root.html](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/verify-root.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#app-proofs)App Proofs

App Proof: a signature by an enclave ephemeral key to prove application-specific facts about functionality. An app proof, when combined with a boot proof, proves that your request was processed:

- by the enclave ephemeral key named in the AWS attestation document
- inside of an AWS Nitro Enclave whose attestation chain verifies to the AWS Nitro root
- with PCR measurements, including the live manifest/key commitment, that match the approved QOS manifest envelope
- with a standalone QOS manifest that is consistent with the approved manifest envelope

This is a cryptographic self-consistency and AWS enclave authenticity claim. It is not, by itself, a global proof that a manifest set is the canonical Turnkey production manifest set. Callers that need that claim must pin or independently obtain the expected manifest policy, operator set, or other Turnkey trust anchor they intend to trust.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#verifying-app-proofs)Verifying App Proofs

Given an app proof, you can request the boot proof for that app proof using `get_boot_proof_for_app_proof`.

To verify the app proof in conjunction with the boot proof, you call `verify(appProof, bootProof)`.
This verification goes through the following steps:

- Verify app proof signature
- Verify the boot proof
- Attestation doc was signed by AWS
- Manifest envelope approvals are internally valid
- Standalone QOS manifest hash matches the manifest envelope hash
- Attestation doc’s `user_data`is the approved manifest envelope hash
- Attestation PCRs match the manifest enclave PCRs and PCR17 live manifest/key commitment

- Verify the app proof / boot proof connection - that the ephemeral keys match

[§](https://docs.rs#attestation-document-verification)Attestation Document Verification

If you have a Turnkey organization you can request a an attestation document from Amazon, signed by a root certificate associated with AWS Nitro Attestation PKI (located in [ aws_root.pem](https://docs.rs/static/aws_root.pem)). This top-level certificate can be downloaded from

[https://aws-nitro-enclaves.amazonaws.com/AWS_NitroEnclaves_Root-G1.zip](https://aws-nitro-enclaves.amazonaws.com/AWS_NitroEnclaves_Root-G1.zip).

You may request a fresh attestation with the `turnkey` CLI (available [here](https://github.com/tkhq/tkcli)):

```
$ turnkey request --host api.turnkey.com --path /public/v1/query/get_attestation --body '{ "organizationId": "<your organization ID>", "enclaveType": "signer" }' --organization <your organization ID>
{
   "attestationDocument": "<base64-encoded attestation document>"
}
```
This crate contains a function to parse and verify this attestation: `parse_and_verify_aws_nitro_attestation`. This returns an `AttestationDoc` containing PCR values. You can display these values like so:

```
use hex;
use turnkey_proofs::parse_and_verify_aws_nitro_attestation;
let attestation_document = "<base64-encoded attestation doc>".to_string();
let attestation = parse_and_verify_aws_nitro_attestation(attestation_document, None)
   .expect("cannot parse and verify attestation document");
// Display PCR values
println!("PCR0: {}", hex::encode(attestation.pcrs.get(&0).unwrap()));
println!("PCR1: {}", hex::encode(attestation.pcrs.get(&1).unwrap()));
println!("PCR2: {}", hex::encode(attestation.pcrs.get(&2).unwrap()));
println!("PCR3: {}", hex::encode(attestation.pcrs.get(&3).unwrap()));
println!("PCR16: {}", hex::encode(attestation.pcrs.get(&16).unwrap()));
println!("PCR17: {}", hex::encode(attestation.pcrs.get(&17).unwrap()));
// Display user data and public key fields
println!("user_data: {}", hex::encode(attestation.user_data.unwrap()));
println!(
   "public_key: {}",
   hex::encode(attestation.public_key.unwrap())
);
```
For full QoS manifest verification of a parsed attestation document, use the
phase-specific helpers re-exported from QoS:
`verify_attestation_doc_against_manifest_live` checks the live/app
manifest/key commitment in PCR17 and is almost always the right choice for
application proof verification. `verify_attestation_doc_against_manifest_setup`
checks the setup/boot manifest/key commitment in PCR16 for provisioning and
bootstrap flows.

Head over to the [QuorumOS](https://github.com/tkhq/qos) repository if you’re looking to reproduce these PCR values independently.

# locale_config 0.3.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/locale_config/0.3.0

`locale_config`

Remembers locale configuration per-thread and per-process and initializes the values by inspecting the system for user preferences.

## Installation

You can depend on this library by adding `locale_config` to your Cargo dependencies:

```
[]
 = "*"
```
Usually it is not recommended to depend on `*`, but in this case it is
important that incompatible version requirements don't cause multiple
versions to be pulled in the final binary, so I do recommend it here and
promise I will maintain good compatibility. Just please don't add traits to
the types defined here to avoid conflicts with potential future methods.

## Using

Usually you want to use this indirectly via a localization crate like
`locale`. However if you need to work with the identifier itself, or you need
to override it, use

```
current
```
to find what you should be using at any given point in the application,

```
set_current
```
to override it for current thread and

```
set_global_default
```
to override it for new threads.

In case you need to access the initial value, you'll find it under

```
user_default
```
The value may contain language tags specific for various localization
aspects, called categories, and fallbacks. The `Locale::tags_for` method will
take care of selecting relevant tags for you. For preferred language of
translations, use

```
current.tags_for
```
For formatting, use categories `"numeric"` for numbers, `"time"` for date and
time and `"monetary"` for money amounts. And use `"collate"` for collation.

Note that this crate does not itself provide any translation, formatting nor
collation functionality. Formatting and collation will be provided by
`locale` crate, translation has multiple available implementations.

See full documentation on [ or ](https://docs.rs/locale_config/)[github](https://rust-locale.github.io/locale_config/locale_config/).

## Supported systems

-
**Unix:**Using the POSIX standard environment variables`LANG`,`LC_*`and`LANGUAGES`. The variables are recognized on all systems and take precedence on most of them.
-
**Windows:**Vista and newer- Uses API available from Vista and Server 2008 only.
- The `GetUserPreferredUILanguages`is only available for desktop, but not store applications. Store applications should have equivalent functionality, but I didn't try accessing it from Rust yet.
- Customization to individual locale elements done in “Regional and Language options” (digits, calendar, decimal and thousand separator etc.) are not detected (yet).
- Not well tested.

-
**OS X:**Reads setting from`NSLocale`, can be overridden by setting the Unix environment variables.
-
**CGI:**The`HTTP_ACCEPT_LANGUAGE`environment variable is used if detected. Hopefully it is specific enough to the CGI environment that it can be used whenever detected.

## Changelog

### 0.3.0

- Support OS X `NSLocale`. Thanks Sophie Tauchert (@999eagle).

### 0.2.3

- Try support getting locale in emscripten targets in browser. Unfortunately the emscripten targets seem to have broken in cross meanwhile, so they are not being tested.
- Update to winapi 0.3.
- Update ro regex 1.0.

### 0.2.2

- Update dependencies: regex 0.2.

### 0.2.1

- Interpret some overrides that can be set on Windows in Region and Language dialog, namely: group, decimal and list separators, first day of week, 12/24-hour time, measurement system, (decimal) number system, to an extent negative monetary value format (only whether to use parenthesized format or not) and to an extent date format (if ISO-8601 variant is selected).

### 0.2.0

- Changed error handling to proper error type.

### 0.1.1

- Added basic Windows support.

### 0.1.0

- Initial version, with Unix and CGI support.

# locale_config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/locale_config/0.3.0/target-redirect/locale_config/

## Expand description

Global locale instances and system inspection.

This is an auxiliary crate for i18n solutions that:

- Holds the appropriate default instances of locale.
- Inspects the system for the initial values.

You don’t want to use it directly, but instead use an internationalisation crate like [locale](https://crates.io/crates/locale).

This crate is separate and intentionally minimal so that multiple i18n crates or multiple versions of one that get into the application still share the current locale setting.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Language](https://docs.rs/struct.LanguageRange.html)- Range
- Language and culture identifier.
- [Locale](https://docs.rs/struct.Locale.html)
- Locale configuration.
- [Tags](https://docs.rs/struct.Tags.html)
- Iterator over `LanguageRange`s for all categories in a`Locale`
- [TagsFor](https://docs.rs/struct.TagsFor.html)
- Iterator over `LanguageRange`s for specific category in a`Locale`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Errors that may be returned by `locale_config`.

[31](https://docs.rs#31)// ------------------------------ LANGUAGE RANGE ---------------------------------
[32](https://docs.rs#32)
[33](https://docs.rs#33)/// Language and culture identifier.
[34](https://docs.rs#34)///
[35](https://docs.rs#35)/// This object holds a [RFC4647] extended language range.
[36](https://docs.rs#36)///
[37](https://docs.rs#37)/// The internal data may be owned or shared from object with lifetime `'a`. The lifetime can be
[38](https://docs.rs#38)/// extended using the `into_static()` method, which internally clones the data as needed.
[39](https://docs.rs#39)///
[40](https://docs.rs#40)/// # Syntax
[41](https://docs.rs#41)///
[42](https://docs.rs#42)/// The range is composed of `-`-separated alphanumeric subtags, possibly replaced by `*`s. It
[43](https://docs.rs#43)/// might be empty.
[44](https://docs.rs#44)///
[45](https://docs.rs#45)/// In agreement with [RFC4647], this object only requires that the tag matches:
[46](https://docs.rs#46)///
[47](https://docs.rs#47)/// ```ebnf
[48](https://docs.rs#48)/// language_tag = (alpha{1,8} | "*")
[49](https://docs.rs#49)///                ("-" (alphanum{1,8} | "*"))*
[50](https://docs.rs#50)/// ```
[51](https://docs.rs#51)///
[52](https://docs.rs#52)/// The exact interpretation is up to the downstream localization provider, but it expected that
[53](https://docs.rs#53)/// it will be matched against a normalized [RFC5646] language tag, which has the structure:
[54](https://docs.rs#54)///
[55](https://docs.rs#55)/// ```ebnf
[56](https://docs.rs#56)/// language_tag    = language
[57](https://docs.rs#57)///                   ("-" script)?
[58](https://docs.rs#58)///                   ("-" region)?
[59](https://docs.rs#59)///                   ("-" variant)*
[60](https://docs.rs#60)///                   ("-" extension)*
[61](https://docs.rs#61)///                   ("-" private)?
[62](https://docs.rs#62)///
[63](https://docs.rs#63)/// language        = alpha{2,3} ("-" alpha{3}){0,3}
[64](https://docs.rs#64)///
[65](https://docs.rs#65)/// script          = aplha{4}
[66](https://docs.rs#66)///
[67](https://docs.rs#67)/// region          = alpha{2}
[68](https://docs.rs#68)///                 | digit{3}
[69](https://docs.rs#69)///
[70](https://docs.rs#70)/// variant         = alphanum{5,8}
[71](https://docs.rs#71)///                 | digit alphanum{3}
[72](https://docs.rs#72)///
[73](https://docs.rs#73)/// extension       = [0-9a-wyz] ("-" alphanum{2,8})+
[74](https://docs.rs#74)///
[75](https://docs.rs#75)/// private         = "x" ("-" alphanum{1,8})+
[76](https://docs.rs#76)/// ```
[77](https://docs.rs#77)///
[78](https://docs.rs#78)///  * `language` is an [ISO639] 2-letter or, where not defined, 3-letter code. A code for
[79](https://docs.rs#79)///     macro-language might be followed by code of specific dialect.
[80](https://docs.rs#80)///  * `script` is an [ISO15924] 4-letter code.
[81](https://docs.rs#81)///  * `region` is either an [ISO3166] 2-letter code or, for areas other than countries, [UN M.49]
[82](https://docs.rs#82)///    3-digit numeric code.
[83](https://docs.rs#83)///  * `variant` is a string indicating variant of the language.
[84](https://docs.rs#84)///  * `extension` and `private` define additional options. The private part has same structure as
[85](https://docs.rs#85)///    the Unicode [`-u-` extension][u_ext]. Available options are documented for the facets that
[86](https://docs.rs#86)///    use them.
[87](https://docs.rs#87)///
[88](https://docs.rs#88)/// The values obtained by inspecting the system are normalized according to those rules.
[89](https://docs.rs#89)///
[90](https://docs.rs#90)/// The content will be case-normalized as recommended in [RFC5646] §2.1.1, namely:
[91](https://docs.rs#91)///
[92](https://docs.rs#92)///  * `language` is written in lowercase,
[93](https://docs.rs#93)///  * `script` is written with first capital,
[94](https://docs.rs#94)///  * `country` is written in uppercase and
[95](https://docs.rs#95)///  * all other subtags are written in lowercase.
[96](https://docs.rs#96)///
[97](https://docs.rs#97)/// When detecting system configuration, additional options that may be generated under the
[98](https://docs.rs#98)/// [`-u-` extension][u_ext] currently are:
[99](https://docs.rs#99)///
[100](https://docs.rs#100)/// * `cf` — Currency format (`account` for parenthesized negative values, `standard` for minus
[101](https://docs.rs#101)///   sign).
[102](https://docs.rs#102)/// * `fw` — First day of week (`mon` to `sun`).
[103](https://docs.rs#103)/// * `hc` — Hour cycle (`h12` for 1–12, `h23` for 0–23).
[104](https://docs.rs#104)/// * `ms` — Measurement system (`metric` or `ussystem`).
[105](https://docs.rs#105)/// * `nu` — Numbering system—only decimal systems are currently used.
[106](https://docs.rs#106)/// * `va` — Variant when locale is specified in Unix format and the tag after `@` does not
[107](https://docs.rs#107)///   correspond to any variant defined in [Language subtag registry].
[108](https://docs.rs#108)///
[109](https://docs.rs#109)/// And under the `-x-` extension, following options are defined:
[110](https://docs.rs#110)///
[111](https://docs.rs#111)/// * `df` — Date format:
[112](https://docs.rs#112)///
[113](https://docs.rs#113)///     * `iso`: Short date should be in ISO format of `yyyy-MM-dd`.
[114](https://docs.rs#114)///
[115](https://docs.rs#115)///     For example `-df-iso`.
[116](https://docs.rs#116)///
[117](https://docs.rs#117)/// * `dm` — Decimal separator for monetary:
[118](https://docs.rs#118)///
[119](https://docs.rs#119)///     Followed by one or more Unicode codepoints in hexadecimal. For example `-dm-002d` means to
[120](https://docs.rs#120)///     use comma.
[121](https://docs.rs#121)///
[122](https://docs.rs#122)/// * `ds` — Decimal separator for numbers:
[123](https://docs.rs#123)///
[124](https://docs.rs#124)///     Followed by one or more Unicode codepoints in hexadecimal. For example `-ds-002d` means to
[125](https://docs.rs#125)///     use comma.
[126](https://docs.rs#126)///
[127](https://docs.rs#127)/// * `gm` — Group (thousand) separator for monetary:
[128](https://docs.rs#128)///
[129](https://docs.rs#129)///     Followed by one or more Unicode codepoints in hexadecimal. For example `-dm-00a0` means to
[130](https://docs.rs#130)///     use non-breaking space.
[131](https://docs.rs#131)///
[132](https://docs.rs#132)/// * `gs` — Group (thousand) separator for numbers:
[133](https://docs.rs#133)///
[134](https://docs.rs#134)///     Followed by one or more Unicode codepoints in hexadecimal. For example `-ds-00a0` means to
[135](https://docs.rs#135)///     use non-breaking space.
[136](https://docs.rs#136)///
[137](https://docs.rs#137)/// * `ls` — List separator:
[138](https://docs.rs#138)///
[139](https://docs.rs#139)///     Followed by one or more Unicode codepoints in hexadecimal. For example, `-ds-003b` means to
[140](https://docs.rs#140)///     use a semicolon.
[141](https://docs.rs#141)///
[142](https://docs.rs#142)/// [RFC5646]: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5646.txt
[143](https://docs.rs#143)/// [RFC4647]: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4647.txt
[144](https://docs.rs#144)/// [ISO639]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_639
[145](https://docs.rs#145)/// [ISO15924]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_15924
[146](https://docs.rs#146)/// [ISO3166]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166
[147](https://docs.rs#147)/// [UN M.49]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_M.49
[148](https://docs.rs#148)/// [u_ext]: http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr35/#u_Extension
[149](https://docs.rs#149)/// [Language subtag registry]: https://www.iana.org/assignments/language-subtag-registry/language-subtag-registry
[150](https://docs.rs#150)#[derive(Clone,Debug,Eq,Hash,PartialEq)]
[151](https://docs.rs#151)pub struct LanguageRange<'a> {
[152](https://docs.rs#152)    language: Cow<'a, str>
[153](https://docs.rs#153)}
[154](https://docs.rs#154)
[155](https://docs.rs#155)lazy_static! {
[156](https://docs.rs#156)    static ref REGULAR_LANGUAGE_RANGE_REGEX: Regex = Regex::new(r"(?x) ^
[157](https://docs.rs#157)        (?P<language> (?:
[158](https://docs.rs#158)            [[:alpha:]]{2,3} (?: - [[:alpha:]]{3} ){0,3}
[159](https://docs.rs#159)            | \* ))
[160](https://docs.rs#160)        (?P<script> - (?: [[:alpha:]]{4} | \* ))?
[161](https://docs.rs#161)        (?P<region> - (?: [[:alpha:]]{2} | [[:digit:]]{3} | \* ))?
[162](https://docs.rs#162)        (?P<rest> (?: - (?: [[:alnum:]]{1,8} | \* ))*)
[163](https://docs.rs#163)    $ ").unwrap();
[164](https://docs.rs#164)    static ref LANGUAGE_RANGE_REGEX: Regex = Regex::new(r"(?x) ^
[165](https://docs.rs#165)        (?: [[:alpha:]]{1,8} | \* )
[166](https://docs.rs#166)        (?: - (?: [[:alnum:]]{1,8} | \* ))*
[167](https://docs.rs#167)    $ ").unwrap();
[168](https://docs.rs#168)    static ref UNIX_INVARIANT_REGEX: Regex = Regex::new(r"(?ix) ^
[169](https://docs.rs#169)        (?: c | posix )
[170](https://docs.rs#170)        (?: \. (?: [0-9a-zA-Z-]{1,20} ))?
[171](https://docs.rs#171)    $ ").unwrap();
[172](https://docs.rs#172)    static ref UNIX_TAG_REGEX: Regex = Regex::new(r"(?ix) ^
[173](https://docs.rs#173)        (?P<language> [[:alpha:]]{2,3} )
[174](https://docs.rs#174)        (?: _  (?P<region> [[:alpha:]]{2} | [[:digit:]]{3} ))?
[175](https://docs.rs#175)        (?: \. (?P<encoding> [0-9a-zA-Z-]{1,20} ))?
[176](https://docs.rs#176)        (?: @  (?P<variant> [[:alnum:]]{1,20} ))?
[177](https://docs.rs#177)    $ ").unwrap();
[178](https://docs.rs#178)}
[179](https://docs.rs#179)
[180](https://docs.rs#180)fn is_owned<'a, T: ToOwned + ?Sized>(c: &Cow<'a, T>) -> bool {
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    match *c {
[182](https://docs.rs#182)        Cow::Owned(_) => true,
[183](https://docs.rs#183)        Cow::Borrowed(_) => false,
[184](https://docs.rs#184)    }
[185](https://docs.rs#185)}
[186](https://docs.rs#186)
[187](https://docs.rs#187)fn canon_lower<'a>(o: Option<&'a str>) -> Cow<'a, str> {
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    match o {
[189](https://docs.rs#189)        None => Cow::Borrowed(""),
[190](https://docs.rs#190)        Some(s) =>
[191](https://docs.rs#191)            if s.chars().any(char::is_uppercase) {
[192](https://docs.rs#192)                Cow::Owned(s.to_ascii_lowercase())
[193](https://docs.rs#193)            } else {
[194](https://docs.rs#194)                Cow::Borrowed(s)
[195](https://docs.rs#195)            },
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    }
[197](https://docs.rs#197)}
[198](https://docs.rs#198)
[199](https://docs.rs#199)fn canon_script<'a>(o: Option<&'a str>) -> Cow<'a, str> {
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    assert!(o.map_or(true, |s| s.len() >= 2 && &s[0..1] == "-"));
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    match o {
[202](https://docs.rs#202)        None => Cow::Borrowed(""),
[203](https://docs.rs#203)        Some(s) =>
[204](https://docs.rs#204)            if s[1..2].chars().next().unwrap().is_uppercase() &&
[205](https://docs.rs#205)               s[2..].chars().all(char::is_lowercase) {
[206](https://docs.rs#206)                Cow::Borrowed(s)
[207](https://docs.rs#207)            } else {
[208](https://docs.rs#208)                Cow::Owned(String::from("-") +
[209](https://docs.rs#209)                           s[1..2].to_ascii_uppercase().as_ref() +
[210](https://docs.rs#210)                           s[2..].to_ascii_lowercase().as_ref())
[211](https://docs.rs#211)            },
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    }
[213](https://docs.rs#213)}
[214](https://docs.rs#214)
[215](https://docs.rs#215)fn canon_upper<'a>(o: Option<&'a str>) -> Cow<'a, str> {
[216](https://docs.rs#216)    assert!(o.map_or(true, |s| s.len() > 1 && &s[0..1] == "-"));
[217](https://docs.rs#217)    match o {
[218](https://docs.rs#218)        None => Cow::Borrowed(""),
[219](https://docs.rs#219)        Some(s) =>
[220](https://docs.rs#220)            if s.chars().any(char::is_lowercase) {
[221](https://docs.rs#221)                Cow::Owned(s.to_ascii_uppercase())
[222](https://docs.rs#222)            } else {
[223](https://docs.rs#223)                Cow::Borrowed(s)
[224](https://docs.rs#224)            },
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    }
[226](https://docs.rs#226)}
[227](https://docs.rs#227)
[228](https://docs.rs#228)impl<'a> LanguageRange<'a> {
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    /// Construct LanguageRange from string, with normalization.
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    ///
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    /// LanguageRange must follow the [RFC4647] syntax.
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    /// It will be case-normalized as recommended in [RFC5646] §2.1.1, namely:
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    ///
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    ///  * `language`, if recognized, is written in lowercase,
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    ///  * `script`, if recognized, is written with first capital,
[236](https://docs.rs#236)    ///  * `country`, if recognized, is written in uppercase and
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    ///  * all other subtags are written in lowercase.
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    ///
[239](https://docs.rs#239)    /// [RFC5646]: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5646.txt
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    /// [RFC4647]: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4647.txt
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    pub fn new(lt: &'a str) -> Result<LanguageRange> {
[242](https://docs.rs#242)        if lt == "" {
[243](https://docs.rs#243)            return Ok(LanguageRange {
[244](https://docs.rs#244)                language: Cow::Borrowed(lt),
[245](https://docs.rs#245)            });
[246](https://docs.rs#246)        } else if let Some(caps) = REGULAR_LANGUAGE_RANGE_REGEX.captures(lt) {
[247](https://docs.rs#247)            let language = canon_lower(caps.name("language").map(|m| m.as_str()));
[248](https://docs.rs#248)            let script = canon_script(caps.name("script").map(|m| m.as_str()));
[249](https://docs.rs#249)            let region = canon_upper(caps.name("region").map(|m| m.as_str()));
[250](https://docs.rs#250)            let rest = canon_lower(caps.name("rest").map(|m| m.as_str()));
[251](https://docs.rs#251)            if is_owned(&language) ||
[252](https://docs.rs#252)                is_owned(&script) ||
[253](https://docs.rs#253)                is_owned(®ion) ||
[254](https://docs.rs#254)                is_owned(&rest)
[255](https://docs.rs#255)            {
[256](https://docs.rs#256)                return Ok(LanguageRange {
[257](https://docs.rs#257)                    language: Cow::Owned(
[258](https://docs.rs#258)                        language.into_owned() +
[259](https://docs.rs#259)                        script.borrow() +
[260](https://docs.rs#260)                        region.borrow() +
[261](https://docs.rs#261)                        rest.borrow()),
[262](https://docs.rs#262)                });
[263](https://docs.rs#263)            } else {
[264](https://docs.rs#264)                return Ok(LanguageRange {
[265](https://docs.rs#265)                    language: Cow::Borrowed(lt),
[266](https://docs.rs#266)                });
[267](https://docs.rs#267)            }
[268](https://docs.rs#268)        } else if LANGUAGE_RANGE_REGEX.is_match(lt) {
[269](https://docs.rs#269)            return Ok(LanguageRange {
[270](https://docs.rs#270)                language: canon_lower(Some(lt)),
[271](https://docs.rs#271)            });
[272](https://docs.rs#272)        } else {
[273](https://docs.rs#273)            return Err(Error::NotWellFormed);
[274](https://docs.rs#274)        }
[275](https://docs.rs#275)    }
[276](https://docs.rs#276)
[277](https://docs.rs#277)    /// Return LanguageRange for the invariant locale.
[278](https://docs.rs#278)    ///
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    /// Invariant language is identified simply by empty string.
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    pub fn invariant() -> LanguageRange<'static> {
[281](https://docs.rs#281)        LanguageRange { language: Cow::Borrowed("") }
[282](https://docs.rs#282)    }
[283](https://docs.rs#283)
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    /// Clone the internal data to extend lifetime.
[285](https://docs.rs#285)    pub fn into_static(self) -> LanguageRange<'static> {
[286](https://docs.rs#286)        LanguageRange {
[287](https://docs.rs#287)            language: Cow::Owned(self.language.into_owned())
[288](https://docs.rs#288)        }
[289](https://docs.rs#289)    }
[290](https://docs.rs#290)
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    /// Create new instance sharing the internal data.
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    pub fn to_shared(&'a self) -> Self {
[293](https://docs.rs#293)        LanguageRange {
[294](https://docs.rs#294)            language: Cow::Borrowed(self.language.borrow())
[295](https://docs.rs#295)        }
[296](https://docs.rs#296)    }
[297](https://docs.rs#297)
[298](https://docs.rs#298)    /// Create language tag from Unix/Linux/GNU locale tag.
[299](https://docs.rs#299)    ///
[300](https://docs.rs#300)    /// Unix locale tags have the form
[301](https://docs.rs#301)    ///
[302](https://docs.rs#302)    /// > *language* [ `_` *region* ] [ `.` *encoding* ] [ `@` *variant* ]
[303](https://docs.rs#303)    ///
[304](https://docs.rs#304)    /// The *language* and *region* have the same format as RFC5646. *Encoding* is not relevant
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    /// here, since Rust always uses Utf-8. That leaves *variant*, which is unfortunately rather
[306](https://docs.rs#306)    /// free-form. So this function will translate known variants to corresponding RFC5646 subtags
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    /// and represent anything else with Unicode POSIX variant (`-u-va-`) extension.
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    ///
[309](https://docs.rs#309)    /// Note: This function is public here for benefit of applications that may come across this
[310](https://docs.rs#310)    /// kind of tags from other sources than system configuration.
[311](https://docs.rs#311)    pub fn from_unix(s: &str) -> Result<LanguageRange<'static>> {
[312](https://docs.rs#312)        if let Some(caps) = UNIX_TAG_REGEX.captures(s) {
[313](https://docs.rs#313)            let src_variant = caps.name("variant").map(|m| m.as_str()).unwrap_or("").to_ascii_lowercase();
[314](https://docs.rs#314)            let mut res = caps.name("language").map(|m| m.as_str()).unwrap().to_ascii_lowercase();
[315](https://docs.rs#315)            let region = caps.name("region").map(|m| m.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
[316](https://docs.rs#316)            let mut script = "";
[317](https://docs.rs#317)            let mut variant = "";
[318](https://docs.rs#318)            let mut uvariant = "";
[319](https://docs.rs#319)            match src_variant.as_ref() {
[320](https://docs.rs#320)            // Variants seen in the wild in GNU LibC (via http://lh.2xlibre.net/) or in Debian
[321](https://docs.rs#321)            // GNU/Linux Stretch system. Treatment of things not found in RFC5646 subtag registry
[322](https://docs.rs#322)            // (http://www.iana.org/assignments/language-subtag-registry/language-subtag-registry)
[323](https://docs.rs#323)            // or CLDR according to notes at https://wiki.openoffice.org/wiki/LocaleMapping.
[324](https://docs.rs#324)            // Dialects:
[325](https://docs.rs#325)                // aa_ER@saaho - NOTE: Can't be found under that name in RFC5646 subtag registry,
[326](https://docs.rs#326)                // but there is language Saho with code ssy, which is likely that thing.
[327](https://docs.rs#327)                "saaho" if res == "aa" => res = String::from("ssy"),
[328](https://docs.rs#328)            // Scripts:
[329](https://docs.rs#329)                // @arabic
[330](https://docs.rs#330)                "arabic" => script = "Arab",
[331](https://docs.rs#331)                // @cyrillic
[332](https://docs.rs#332)                "cyrl" => script = "Cyrl",
[333](https://docs.rs#333)                "cyrillic" => script = "Cyrl",
[334](https://docs.rs#334)                // @devanagari
[335](https://docs.rs#335)                "devanagari" => script = "Deva",
[336](https://docs.rs#336)                // @hebrew
[337](https://docs.rs#337)                "hebrew" => script = "Hebr",
[338](https://docs.rs#338)                // tt@iqtelif
[339](https://docs.rs#339)                // Neither RFC5646 subtag registry nor CLDR knows anything about this, but as best
[340](https://docs.rs#340)                // as I can tell it is Tatar name for Latin (default is Cyrillic).
[341](https://docs.rs#341)                "iqtelif" => script = "Latn",
[342](https://docs.rs#342)                // @Latn
[343](https://docs.rs#343)                "latn" => script = "Latn",
[344](https://docs.rs#344)                // @latin
[345](https://docs.rs#345)                "latin" => script = "Latn",
[346](https://docs.rs#346)                // en@shaw
[347](https://docs.rs#347)                "shaw" => script = "Shaw",
[348](https://docs.rs#348)            // Variants:
[349](https://docs.rs#349)                // sr@ijekavianlatin
[350](https://docs.rs#350)                "ijekavianlatin" => {
[351](https://docs.rs#351)                    script = "Latn";
[352](https://docs.rs#352)                    variant = "ijekavsk";
[353](https://docs.rs#353)                },
[354](https://docs.rs#354)                // sr@ije
[355](https://docs.rs#355)                "ije" => variant = "ijekavsk",
[356](https://docs.rs#356)                // sr@ijekavian
[357](https://docs.rs#357)                "ijekavian" => variant = "ijekavsk",
[358](https://docs.rs#358)                // ca@valencia
[359](https://docs.rs#359)                "valencia" => variant = "valencia",
[360](https://docs.rs#360)            // Currencies:
[361](https://docs.rs#361)                // @euro - NOTE: We follow suite of Java and Openoffice and ignore it, because it
[362](https://docs.rs#362)                // is default for all locales where it sometimes appears now, and because we use
[363](https://docs.rs#363)                // explicit currency in monetary formatting anyway.
[364](https://docs.rs#364)                "euro" => {},
[365](https://docs.rs#365)            // Collation:
[366](https://docs.rs#366)                // gez@abegede - NOTE: This is collation, but CLDR does not have any code for it,
[367](https://docs.rs#367)                // so we for the moment leave it fall through as -u-va- instead of -u-co-.
[368](https://docs.rs#368)            // Anything else:
[369](https://docs.rs#369)                // en@boldquot, en@quot, en@piglatin - just randomish stuff
[370](https://docs.rs#370)                // @cjknarrow - beware, it's gonna end up as -u-va-cjknarro due to lenght limit
[371](https://docs.rs#371)                s if s.len() <= 8 => uvariant = &*s,
[372](https://docs.rs#372)                s => uvariant = &s[0..8], // the subtags are limited to 8 chars, but some are longer
[373](https://docs.rs#373)            };
[374](https://docs.rs#374)            if script != "" {
[375](https://docs.rs#375)                res.push('-');
[376](https://docs.rs#376)                res.push_str(script);
[377](https://docs.rs#377)            }
[378](https://docs.rs#378)            if region != "" {
[379](https://docs.rs#379)                res.push('-');
[380](https://docs.rs#380)                res.push_str(&*region.to_ascii_uppercase());
[381](https://docs.rs#381)            }
[382](https://docs.rs#382)            if variant != "" {
[383](https://docs.rs#383)                res.push('-');
[384](https://docs.rs#384)                res.push_str(variant);
[385](https://docs.rs#385)            }
[386](https://docs.rs#386)            if uvariant != "" {
[387](https://docs.rs#387)                res.push_str("-u-va-");
[388](https://docs.rs#388)                res.push_str(uvariant);
[389](https://docs.rs#389)            }
[390](https://docs.rs#390)            return Ok(LanguageRange {
[391](https://docs.rs#391)                language: Cow::Owned(res)
[392](https://docs.rs#392)            });
[393](https://docs.rs#393)        } else if UNIX_INVARIANT_REGEX.is_match(s) {
[394](https://docs.rs#394)            return Ok(LanguageRange::invariant())
[395](https://docs.rs#395)        } else {
[396](https://docs.rs#396)            return Err(Error::NotWellFormed);
[397](https://docs.rs#397)        }
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    }
[399](https://docs.rs#399)}
[400](https://docs.rs#400)
[401](https://docs.rs#401)impl<'a> AsRef<str> for LanguageRange<'a> {
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    fn as_ref(&self) -> &str {
[403](https://docs.rs#403)        self.language.as_ref()
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    }

[414](https://docs.rs#414)
[415](https://docs.rs#415)/// Locale configuration.
[416](https://docs.rs#416)///
[417](https://docs.rs#417)/// Users may accept several languages in some order of preference and may want to use rules from
[418](https://docs.rs#418)/// different culture for some particular aspect of the program behaviour, and operating systems
[419](https://docs.rs#419)/// allow them to specify this (to various extent).
[420](https://docs.rs#420)///
[421](https://docs.rs#421)/// The `Locale` objects represent the user configuration. They contain:
[422](https://docs.rs#422)///
[423](https://docs.rs#423)///  - The primary `LanguageRange`.
[424](https://docs.rs#424)///  - Optional category-specific overrides.
[425](https://docs.rs#425)///  - Optional fallbacks in case data (usually translations) for the primary language are not
[426](https://docs.rs#426)///    available.
[427](https://docs.rs#427)///
[428](https://docs.rs#428)/// The set of categories is open-ended. The `locale` crate uses five well-known categories
[429](https://docs.rs#429)/// `messages`, `numeric`, `time`, `collate` and `monetary`, but some systems define additional
[430](https://docs.rs#430)/// ones (GNU Linux has additionally `paper`, `name`, `address`, `telephone` and `measurement`) and
[431](https://docs.rs#431)/// these are provided in the user default `Locale` and other libraries can use them.
[432](https://docs.rs#432)///
[433](https://docs.rs#433)/// `Locale` is represented by a `,`-separated sequence of tags in `LanguageRange` syntax, where
[434](https://docs.rs#434)/// all except the first one may be preceded by category name and `=` sign.
[435](https://docs.rs#435)///
[436](https://docs.rs#436)/// The first tag indicates the default locale, the tags prefixed by category names indicate
[437](https://docs.rs#437)/// _overrides_ for those categories and the remaining tags indicate fallbacks.
[438](https://docs.rs#438)///
[439](https://docs.rs#439)/// Note that a syntactically valid value of HTTP `Accept-Language` header is a valid `Locale`. Not
[440](https://docs.rs#440)/// the other way around though due to the presence of category selectors.
[441](https://docs.rs#441)// TODO: Interning
[442](https://docs.rs#442)#[derive(Clone,Debug,Eq,Hash,PartialEq)]
[443](https://docs.rs#443)pub struct Locale {
[444](https://docs.rs#444)    // TODO: Intern the string for performance reasons
[445](https://docs.rs#445)    // XXX: Store pre-split to LanguageTags?
[446](https://docs.rs#446)    inner: String,
[447](https://docs.rs#447)}
[448](https://docs.rs#448)
[449](https://docs.rs#449)lazy_static! {
[450](https://docs.rs#450)    static ref LOCALE_ELEMENT_REGEX: Regex = Regex::new(r"(?ix) ^
[451](https://docs.rs#451)        (?: (?P<category> [[:alpha:]]{1,20} ) = )?
[452](https://docs.rs#452)        (?P<tag> (?: [[:alnum:]] | - | \* )+ )
[453](https://docs.rs#453)    $ ").unwrap();
[454](https://docs.rs#454)}
[455](https://docs.rs#455)
[456](https://docs.rs#456)impl Locale {
[457](https://docs.rs#457)    /// Obtain the user default locale.
[458](https://docs.rs#458)    ///
[459](https://docs.rs#459)    /// This is the locale indicated by operating environment.
[460](https://docs.rs#460)    pub fn user_default() -> Locale {
[461](https://docs.rs#461)        USER_LOCALE.clone()
[462](https://docs.rs#462)    }
[463](https://docs.rs#463)
[464](https://docs.rs#464)    /// Obtain the global default locale.
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    ///
[466](https://docs.rs#466)    /// The global default for `current()` locale. Defaults to `user_default()`.
[467](https://docs.rs#467)    pub fn global_default() -> Locale {
[468](https://docs.rs#468)        GLOBAL_LOCALE.lock().unwrap().clone()
[469](https://docs.rs#469)    }
[470](https://docs.rs#470)
[471](https://docs.rs#471)    /// Change the global default locale.
[472](https://docs.rs#472)    ///
[473](https://docs.rs#473)    /// Setting this overrides the default for new threads and threads that didn't do any
[474](https://docs.rs#474)    /// locale-aware operation yet.
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    pub fn set_global_default(lb: Locale) {
[476](https://docs.rs#476)        *GLOBAL_LOCALE.lock().unwrap() = lb;
[477](https://docs.rs#477)    }
[478](https://docs.rs#478)
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    /// Obtain the current locale of current thread.
[480](https://docs.rs#480)    ///
[481](https://docs.rs#481)    /// Defaults to `global_default()` on first use in each thread.
[482](https://docs.rs#482)    pub fn current() -> Locale {
[483](https://docs.rs#483)        CURRENT_LOCALE.with(|l| l.borrow().clone())
[484](https://docs.rs#484)    }
[485](https://docs.rs#485)
[486](https://docs.rs#486)    /// Change the current locale of current thread.
[487](https://docs.rs#487)    pub fn set_current(lb: Locale) {
[488](https://docs.rs#488)        CURRENT_LOCALE.with(|l| *l.borrow_mut() = lb);
[489](https://docs.rs#489)    }
[490](https://docs.rs#490)
[491](https://docs.rs#491)    /// Construct locale from the string representation.
[492](https://docs.rs#492)    ///
[493](https://docs.rs#493)    /// `Locale` is represented by a `,`-separated sequence of tags in `LanguageRange` syntax, where
[494](https://docs.rs#494)    /// all except the first one may be preceded by category name and `=` sign.
[495](https://docs.rs#495)    ///
[496](https://docs.rs#496)    /// The first tag indicates the default locale, the tags prefixed by category names indicate
[497](https://docs.rs#497)    /// _overrides_ for those categories and the remaining tags indicate fallbacks.
[498](https://docs.rs#498)    pub fn new(s: &str) -> Result<Locale> {
[499](https://docs.rs#499)        let mut i = s.split(',');
[500](https://docs.rs#500)        let mut res = Locale::from(
[501](https://docs.rs#501)            try!(LanguageRange::new(
[502](https://docs.rs#502)                    i.next().unwrap()))); // NOTE: split "" is (""), not ()
[503](https://docs.rs#503)        for t in i {
[504](https://docs.rs#504)            if let Some(caps) = LOCALE_ELEMENT_REGEX.captures(t) {
[505](https://docs.rs#505)                let tag = try!(LanguageRange::new(
[506](https://docs.rs#506)                        try!(caps.name("tag").map(|m| m.as_str()).ok_or(Error::NotWellFormed))));
[507](https://docs.rs#507)                match caps.name("category").map(|m| m.as_str()) {
[508](https://docs.rs#508)                    Some(cat) => res.add_category(cat.to_ascii_lowercase().as_ref(), &tag),
[509](https://docs.rs#509)                    None => res.add(&tag),
[510](https://docs.rs#510)                }
[511](https://docs.rs#511)            } else {
[512](https://docs.rs#512)                return Err(Error::NotWellFormed);
[513](https://docs.rs#513)            }
[514](https://docs.rs#514)        }
[515](https://docs.rs#515)        return Ok(res);
[516](https://docs.rs#516)    }
[517](https://docs.rs#517)
[518](https://docs.rs#518)    /// Construct invariant locale.
[519](https://docs.rs#519)    ///
[520](https://docs.rs#520)    /// Invariant locale is represented simply with empty string.
[521](https://docs.rs#521)    pub fn invariant() -> Locale {
[522](https://docs.rs#522)        Locale::from(LanguageRange::invariant())
[523](https://docs.rs#523)    }
[524](https://docs.rs#524)
[525](https://docs.rs#525)    /// Append fallback language tag.
[526](https://docs.rs#526)    ///
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    /// Adds fallback to the end of the list.
[528](https://docs.rs#528)    pub fn add(&mut self, tag: &LanguageRange) {
[529](https://docs.rs#529)        for i in self.inner.split(',') {
[530](https://docs.rs#530)            if i == tag.as_ref() {
[531](https://docs.rs#531)                return; // don't add duplicates
[532](https://docs.rs#532)            }
[533](https://docs.rs#533)        }
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        self.inner.push_str(",");
[535](https://docs.rs#535)        self.inner.push_str(tag.as_ref());
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    }
[537](https://docs.rs#537)
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    /// Append category override.
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    ///
[540](https://docs.rs#540)    /// Appending new override for a category that already has one will not replace the existing
[541](https://docs.rs#541)    /// override. This might change in future.
[542](https://docs.rs#542)    pub fn add_category(&mut self, category: &str, tag: &LanguageRange) {
[543](https://docs.rs#543)        if self.inner.split(',').next().unwrap() == tag.as_ref() {
[544](https://docs.rs#544)            return; // don't add useless override equal to the primary tag
[545](https://docs.rs#545)        }
[546](https://docs.rs#546)        for i in self.inner.split(',') {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)            if i.starts_with(category) &&
[548](https://docs.rs#548)                    i[category.len()..].starts_with("=") &&
[549](https://docs.rs#549)                    &i[category.len() + 1..] == tag.as_ref() {
[550](https://docs.rs#550)                return; // don't add duplicates
[551](https://docs.rs#551)            }
[552](https://docs.rs#552)        }
[553](https://docs.rs#553)        self.inner.push_str(",");
[554](https://docs.rs#554)        self.inner.push_str(category);
[555](https://docs.rs#555)        self.inner.push_str("=");
[556](https://docs.rs#556)        self.inner.push_str(tag.as_ref());
[557](https://docs.rs#557)    }
[558](https://docs.rs#558)
[559](https://docs.rs#559)    /// Iterate over `LanguageRange`s in this `Locale`.
[560](https://docs.rs#560)    ///
[561](https://docs.rs#561)    /// Returns tuples of optional category (as string) and corresponding `LanguageRange`. All tags
[562](https://docs.rs#562)    /// in the list are returned, in order of preference.
[563](https://docs.rs#563)    ///
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    /// The iterator is guaranteed to return at least one value.
[565](https://docs.rs#565)    pub fn tags<'a>(&'a self) -> Tags<'a> {
[566](https://docs.rs#566)        Tags { tags: self.inner.split(","), }
[567](https://docs.rs#567)    }
[568](https://docs.rs#568)
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    /// Iterate over `LanguageRange`s in this `Locale` applicable to given category.
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    ///
[571](https://docs.rs#571)    /// Returns `LanguageRange`s in the `Locale` that are applicable to provided category. The tags
[572](https://docs.rs#572)    /// are returned in order of preference, which means the category-specific ones first and then
[573](https://docs.rs#573)    /// the generic ones.
[574](https://docs.rs#574)    ///
[575](https://docs.rs#575)    /// The iterator is guaranteed to return at least one value.
[576](https://docs.rs#576)    pub fn tags_for<'a, 'c>(&'a self, category: &'c str) -> TagsFor<'a, 'c> {
[577](https://docs.rs#577)        let mut tags = self.inner.split(",");
[578](https://docs.rs#578)        while let Some(s) = tags.clone().next() {
[579](https://docs.rs#579)            if s.starts_with(category) && s[category.len()..].starts_with("=") {
[580](https://docs.rs#580)                return TagsFor {
[581](https://docs.rs#581)                    src: self.inner.as_ref(),
[582](https://docs.rs#582)                    tags: tags,
[583](https://docs.rs#583)                    category: Some(category),
[584](https://docs.rs#584)                };
[585](https://docs.rs#585)            }
[586](https://docs.rs#586)            tags.next();
[587](https://docs.rs#587)        }
[588](https://docs.rs#588)        return TagsFor {
[589](https://docs.rs#589)            src: self.inner.as_ref(),
[590](https://docs.rs#590)            tags: self.inner.split(","),
[591](https://docs.rs#591)            category: None,
[592](https://docs.rs#592)        };
[593](https://docs.rs#593)    }
[594](https://docs.rs#594)}

[618](https://docs.rs#618)
[619](https://docs.rs#619)/// Iterator over `LanguageRange`s for all categories in a `Locale`
[620](https://docs.rs#620)///
[621](https://docs.rs#621)/// Returns tuples of optional category (as string) and corresponding `LanguageRange`. All tags
[622](https://docs.rs#622)/// in the list are returned, in order of preference.
[623](https://docs.rs#623)///
[624](https://docs.rs#624)/// The iterator is guaranteed to return at least one value.
[625](https://docs.rs#625)pub struct Tags<'a> {
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    tags: std::str::Split<'a, &'static str>,
[627](https://docs.rs#627)}
[628](https://docs.rs#628)
[629](https://docs.rs#629)impl<'a> Iterator for Tags<'a> {
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    type Item = (Option<&'a str>, LanguageRange<'a>);
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
[632](https://docs.rs#632)        if let Some(s) = self.tags.next() {
[633](https://docs.rs#633)            if let Some(i) = s.find('=') {
[634](https://docs.rs#634)                return Some((
[635](https://docs.rs#635)                    Some(&s[..i]),
[636](https://docs.rs#636)                    LanguageRange { language: Cow::Borrowed(&s[i+1..]), }));
[637](https://docs.rs#637)            } else {
[638](https://docs.rs#638)                return Some((
[639](https://docs.rs#639)                    None,
[640](https://docs.rs#640)                    LanguageRange { language: Cow::Borrowed(s), }));
[641](https://docs.rs#641)            }
[642](https://docs.rs#642)        } else {
[643](https://docs.rs#643)            return None;
[644](https://docs.rs#644)        }
[645](https://docs.rs#645)    }
[646](https://docs.rs#646)}
[647](https://docs.rs#647)
[648](https://docs.rs#648)/// Iterator over `LanguageRange`s for specific category in a `Locale`
[649](https://docs.rs#649)///
[650](https://docs.rs#650)/// Returns `LanguageRange`s in the `Locale` that are applicable to provided category. The tags
[651](https://docs.rs#651)/// are returned in order of preference, which means the category-specific ones first and then
[652](https://docs.rs#652)/// the generic ones.
[653](https://docs.rs#653)///
[654](https://docs.rs#654)/// The iterator is guaranteed to return at least one value.
[655](https://docs.rs#655)pub struct TagsFor<'a, 'c> {
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    src: &'a str,
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    tags: std::str::Split<'a, &'static str>,
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    category: Option<&'c str>,
[659](https://docs.rs#659)}
[660](https://docs.rs#660)
[661](https://docs.rs#661)impl<'a, 'c> Iterator for TagsFor<'a, 'c> {
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    type Item = LanguageRange<'a>;
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
[664](https://docs.rs#664)        if let Some(cat) = self.category {
[665](https://docs.rs#665)            while let Some(s) = self.tags.next() {
[666](https://docs.rs#666)                if s.starts_with(cat) && s[cat.len()..].starts_with("=") {
[667](https://docs.rs#667)                    return Some(
[668](https://docs.rs#668)                        LanguageRange { language: Cow::Borrowed(&s[cat.len()+1..]) });
[669](https://docs.rs#669)                }
[670](https://docs.rs#670)            }
[671](https://docs.rs#671)            self.category = None;
[672](https://docs.rs#672)            self.tags = self.src.split(",");
[673](https://docs.rs#673)        }
[674](https://docs.rs#674)        while let Some(s) = self.tags.next() {
[675](https://docs.rs#675)            if s.find('=').is_none() {
[676](https://docs.rs#676)                return Some(
[677](https://docs.rs#677)                    LanguageRange{ language: Cow::Borrowed(s) });
[678](https://docs.rs#678)            }
[679](https://docs.rs#679)        }
[680](https://docs.rs#680)        return None;
[681](https://docs.rs#681)    }

[700](https://docs.rs#700)// NOTE: Cgi-style environment variable HTTP_ACCEPT_LANGUAGE is unlikely to be defined at any other

[715](https://docs.rs#715)

[719](https://docs.rs#719)
[720](https://docs.rs#720)static INITIALISERS: &'static [fn() -> Option<Locale>] = &[
[721](https://docs.rs#721)    cgi::system_locale,
[722](https://docs.rs#722)    unix::system_locale,
[723](https://docs.rs#723)    #[cfg(target_family = "windows")] win32::system_locale,
[724](https://docs.rs#724)    #[cfg(target_os = "emscripten")] emscripten::system_locale,
[725](https://docs.rs#725)	#[cfg(target_os = "macos")] macos::system_locale,
[726](https://docs.rs#726)];
[727](https://docs.rs#727)
[728](https://docs.rs#728)fn system_locale() -> Locale {
[729](https://docs.rs#729)    for f in INITIALISERS {
[730](https://docs.rs#730)        if let Some(l) = f() {
[731](https://docs.rs#731)            return l;
[732](https://docs.rs#732)        }
[733](https://docs.rs#733)    }
[734](https://docs.rs#734)    return Locale::invariant();
